Chief Executive’s Monthly Management Report – 31st July 2026
 
 
A Chara,  
 
I enclose the above report for your statutory consideration, this report has also been prepared under Section 136 & 
138 of the Local Government Act, 2001. The attached report is the Chief Executive’s Monthly Management Report for 
July 2026, detailing activities, updates, and progress across various departments of Louth County Council.  
 
1. Finance and System Support 
o 
Expenditure to 31 July 2026 was €103.5m (51% of annual budget). Housing, roads, and environmental 
services are the largest spend areas. 
o 
Income to 31 July 2026 was €111m (55% of annual budget), with full rates demand already invoiced. 
o 
Budget 2027: Public consultation on Local Property Tax is underway. 
o 
ICT: 
▪ 11% of inbound emails flagged as potentially harmful. 
▪ Cybersecurity training focused on QR code and URL risks. 
▪ Dowdallshill Graveyard Map Viewer saw a spike in use during the Blessing of the Graves. 
2. Economic Delivery 
• 
Economic Development: 
o 
Shopfront Improvement Grant Scheme open until October. 
o 
Age Friendly Business Accreditation ongoing. 
• 
Tourism: 
o

o

•

o

•

o

• 
Planning: 
o 
103 planning applications received in June, 74 valid, 68 applications determined, 17.65% refused. 
o 
10 enforcement complaints investigated in June; 27 cases closed through negotiation.

• 
Roads & Maintenance: 
o

Ardee, Drogheda, and South Louth.

•

188 litter investigations, 21 fixed penalty notices in July.

o

The above highlights the breadth of activity and progress across all directorates, reflecting Louth County Council’s

Louth County Council team.

 Budget 2027 - Local Property Tax (LPT) Public 
Consultation 
 
The budget process for 2027 has begun with the 
advertising of the Local Property Tax Public 
Consultation in July. The deadline for submissions 
from the public is Friday 21st of August 2026. 
 
The report will go to you, the members, at the 
September meeting where you can decide to set a 
local adjustment factor within the range of +25% to 
– 15% of the basic rate or may decide not to adjust 
the basic rate. If the rate is varied upwards 100% of 
the additional income will be available for the 
authority’s own use. Similarly, if the rate is varied 
downwards the loss of income will be reflected in 
reduced LPT funding to the authority.

Suíomh Gréasáin Comhairle Chontae Lú / Louth County Council Website 
 
Website analytics for July indicate continued strong engagement with the Council's online services. While overall 
visitor numbers remained stable, users spent longer on the website, with average visit duration increasing by 
11.4% to 3 minutes and 26 seconds. Visitors also interacted more actively with online resources, with significant 
increases in document downloads, website searches and links to external services. A reduction in bounce rate 
suggests that users are successfully navigating between pages and accessing the information and services they 
require, reinforcing the website's role as a key self-service channel for the public

Entry Channel Types 
 
Most website visitors accessed www.louthcoco.ie directly during July 2026, demonstrating strong public 
recognition of the Council website as a trusted source of information and services. Search engines also remained 
a significant source of traffic, reflecting the importance of the website's visibility in online search results. The 
continued presence of visits originating from social media, referral websites and AI-powered assistants highlights 
the growing range of digital channels through which residents discover and access Council services. 
 
Cyber Security Training  
 
The July Cyber Security Awareness training highlighted the risks associated with QR codes and shortened 
URLs, which can hide the true destination of a link and be exploited by cybercriminals to steal personal 
information, financial details, or install malware. Staff were reminded to remain vigilant, use tools that preview 
QR code destinations or expand shortened URLs, and verify suspicious links through a trusted source before 
opening them. The key message was simple: if you cannot confidently identify where a link or QR code will 
take you, do not trust it

Digitise Drogheda 
The July edition of the Digitise Drogheda series was 
a resounding success.  This series, delivered 
through a partnership between Drogheda & District 
Chamber of Commerce, Drogheda Digital Hub and 
the Local Enterprise Office Louth, has attracted a full 
house on each occasion and is generating 
outstanding feedback from participants.  The 
initiative was developed to provide local businesses 
with practical, accessible digital skills and expert 
guidance to support growth, competitiveness and 
digital transformation. 
 
Hosted at the Drogheda Digital Hub, the July 
programme featured three highly engaging sessions 
delivered by experienced industry professionals, 
each focusing on a key aspect of business 
digitalisation.  The first was held on the 1st July and 
explored how small businesses can harness AI tools 
to improve productivity, streamline operations, 
enhance customer engagement and identify new 
growth opportunities.  Attendees gained practical 
insights into the real-world applications of artificial 
intelligence and left with actionable ideas they could 
implement within their own organisations. 
 
On 8th July, businesses returned to the Hub for 
Social Media Strategies That Generate Enquiries, 
delivered by Colm Hanratty of Six-Two Digital, 
Drogheda.  The session focused on developing 
effective social media approaches that move beyond 
likes and follows to generate genuine business leads 
and customer enquiries.  Participants learned 
practical techniques for creating engaging content, 
understanding their audience and converting online 
engagement into measurable business outcomes. 
 
The final July workshop took place on 15th July, with 
Keith Byrne of Create 108 leading a session on 
Website and Google Fundamentals.  This popular 
workshop provided businesses with a clear 
understanding of the essential elements required for 
an effective online presence.  Topics included 
website best practice, search visibility, Google 
Business Profile optimisation and the key factors 
that help customers find and engage with 
businesses online. 
 
The strong attendance across all three workshops 
highlights the growing demand among local 
businesses for practical digital skills delivered in an 
accessible 
and 
supportive 
environment.  
Participants welcomed the opportunity to learn 
directly from local experts, network with fellow 
business owners and gain knowledge that could be 
applied immediately within their organisations. 
 
The success of the July programme reinforces the 
value of collaborative initiatives such as Digitise 
Drogheda, which was developed in response to the 
need for practical, locally delivered digital supports 
for SMEs.  Through the combined efforts of 
Drogheda & District Chamber of Commerce, 
Drogheda Digital Hub and Local Enterprise Office 
Louth, local businesses are being equipped with the 
tools and knowledge needed to embrace digital 
technologies, 
strengthen 
competitiveness 
and 
prepare for future growth.  Two more sessions are 
planned for August and already have a huge number
